title: Speculative-router beacon & acceptance signalchain with tiered failover
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight runtime component (the 'beacon') that emits early acceptance signals for speculative decode candidates, drives kernel-aware routing decisions, and enforces a tiered failover policy when acceptance confidence is low.

Scope: design and implement the beacon signalchain, integrate it with existing prefill/decode scheduler, add acceptance metric primitives to runtime telemetry, and ship a fallback policy that meets SLA constraints. This ticket covers runtime-side design, API contract for the beacon signals, instrumentation, unit/integration tests, and an initial canary rollout plan. UI/Console work and long-term model pruning are tracked separately.

Design summary:
- Beacon role: after prefill (or short prefill probe), runtime produces a compact acceptance beacon containing: prefix-likelihood delta, per-kernel latency estimate, KV-cache hit indicator, and short confidence vector (3 numbers). Beacons are produced within prefill completion path and are non-blocking.
- Routing: router receives beacon and scores candidate models (primary, fast-quant, fallback-CPU) using a cost model combining estimated remaining latency, token-cost delta, and acceptance probability. Kernel affinity is considered: if kernel for a higher-accuracy model has high setup cost for current sequence length, prefer a lower-cost variant.
- Acceptance metrics: runtime exposes: beacon_accept_prob, beacon_latency_ms, postprefill_revision_rate, and fallback_activation_count. We add per-route histograms and percentile SLOs. Acceptance is a moving-window probability calibrated with offline evaluation sets.
- Fallback policy (tiered):
  * Tier 0 (fast-path): if beacon_accept_prob >= 0.92 and estimated latency <= route SLO, commit speculative decode result immediately.
  * Tier 1 (deferred-commit): if 0.75 <= prob < 0.92, continue with speculative decode in fast model but keep a background decode on primary model; commit whichever finishes first or meets secondary acceptance thresholds.
  * Tier 2 (failover): if prob < 0.75, route directly to primary model (no speculative decode).
- Safety/rollback: any time the post-commit quality checker (async eval bogie) flags regressions > 1% on selected prompt set, we immediately increase Tier thresholds conservatively and pause rollout.

Runtime changes required:
1) Beacon struct (compact proto): small, fixed-size payload (under 128 bytes) emitted by prefill.
2) Router API: new non-blocking call route.evaluateBeacon(beacon, candidateSet) -> score list.
3) Scheduler: update prefill/decode scheduler to support background primary decode in Tier 1 and to manage resource accounting for background decodes.
4) Telemetry: add acceptance-related spans and counters; surface 1/5/50/95/99 p50-p99 latency buckets by model and kernel tag.
5) Kernel selection hook: router must receive kernel startup cost estimates (from kernel manager) to factor into routing decisions for short sequences.

Trade-offs considered:
- Latency vs. cost: Tier 1 increases overall GPU time due to background decodes but reduces visible quality regressions. We will gate Tier 1 by per-customer cost budget and provide a config toggle per deployment.
- Complexity vs. speed: beacon must be tiny to avoid slowing prefill. We keep the signal vector minimal and rely on server-side cached calibration models.
- Calibration drift: acceptance probabilities are calibrated offline; runtime will auto-correct using lightweight online isotonic updates to avoid large drift windows.

Testing & verification:
- Unit tests for beacon creation and router scoring heuristics.
- Integration test: synthetic workload with deterministic accept/reject oracle to verify Tier behavior.
- Canary: 1% of traffic in staging -> 5% in a canary prod region, monitor beacon_accept_prob, fallback_activation_count, user-facing latency p95, and quality regression alarms.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: land beacon proto and telemetry primitives behind feature flag.
- Week 1: implement router scoring and Tier 0 fast-path, internal staging test.
- Week 2: implement Tier 1 background decode and kernel-cost integration; run extended end-to-end load test.
- Week 3: canary rollout (5%) with close monitoring; prepare rollback automation.
- Week 4: expand to 25% then 100% if metrics OK.

Operational runbook (short):
- If post-commit error rate > threshold or quality regression detected, flip feature flag to disable Tier 1 and Tier 0 commit; system reverts to direct primary routing.
- If GPU exhaustion observed in background decode wave, reduce Tier 1 concurrency cap for the workload.

Open questions:
- Should we include a small RL-tuned scoring model in router, or keep scoring linear and interpretable? (Prefer linear initially for debuggability.)
- How to expose per-customer opt-out and budget gating in the control plane? (Follow-up PM ticket.)

Deliverables: beacon proto, router.evaluateBeacon RPC, scheduler changes, telemetry dashboards, integration tests, canary rollout plan, runbook.
